what_happened: Scene layout 8 / style 8: double-basin steel sink, gooseneck spout with a small separate lever handle at the right of the spout base; colander with lettuce on the counter to the right of the sink (off the agent view). Stage 0: the gripper reached the lever at 116 and stayed on it almost continuously until 594 (touch 116-337, 365-594), fingers open. The wrist view shows the lever between the fingers and barely moving 116-340 (handle 0.00 rad); from ~380 it creeps toward the left finger (0.01 at 384, 0.09-0.14 at 448-576). At 562-583 the fingers closed on nothing and the arm pulled away, dragging the lever to 0.29 rad (592-608), short of the 0.40 rad water-on threshold. No stream is visible at any point. 620-1100: the arm rose and the wrist camera looked down at the sink and counter from above (colander visible at 720-760 and 1048), without approaching the lettuce or the lever again. Stage 1 never started (water off, washed_time 0).
causal_chain: lever contacted 116-594 (~480 steps; typical whole stage 0 is 253, and the L8 success s22 turned the same lever 0->0.50 in ~50 steps of contact) -> lever only pushed to 0.29 rad (< 0.40) when the arm withdrew at ~594 -> water never on -> arm wandered above the sink 620-1100 -> no lettuce washing possible
self_recovery: none: after leaving the lever at 0.29 rad it never returned to it, and it did not try the lettuce either.
official_criterion_notes: Consistent with the video: no water stream at 0.29 rad. The packet's close_events (562 and 583, on_nothing) are the fingers closing as the arm left the lever.
uncertain_about: Why the lever moved so little in ~480 steps of contact; from the wrist view the fingers rest on the lever and push it only slightly. The jump from 0.14 to 0.29 seems to come from the withdrawal motion.
